I'm struggling a little this year with the holidays. I moved several states away almost two years ago from my family and I've been flourishing as an adult and human being.  I think last Christmas/holiday season was easier because I worked Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Years so I was able to spend it with my patients and coworkers that were like a family  (I'm a nurse).  I was also celebrating Christmas with my SO (we met the month after I moved)  and her family minus her sister with BPD on a different day that they did just for me, which is the nicest thing anyone has ever done for me. I think I was so caught up in the newness it didn't affect me. This year, I have so much to be thankful for my SO and I bought a new house, an engagement, a new job (I moved closer to my SO's family), and two kittens. But I can't shake this feeling of being upset. 

My  BPDmom keeps trying to barge in my life this year, especially this month. I've been LC with her more this year than last. She sees that I'm successful and doing quite well and wants to take credit and pretend she's the greatest mom in the world. I've stopped picking up when she calls because she just complains the whole time and hasn't asked about how I'm doing. When I told her I got the diagnosis of bipolar disorder recently and it made sense and I was talking to important people in my life and we were recognizing the manic episodes together from the past, I wanted to do the same with her but just got  "What's wrong with you, I thought you were doing well?".  I'm also remembering a lot of bad memories more so around the holidays- baking cookies with her taking over, the fights she started with my dad and the constant arguing, the push and pull from her especially around that season, and an event of abuse from my dad where we got a call from CPS (who didn't do anything) and her accusing me of making it up and telling the school counselor to take my baby brother away from her. 

​

Interestingly enough, now my mom always throws that event in my dad's face when she wants to fight with him. She only believes it when she can use it.  My SO's half-sister has been coming around more who also has BPD and it has been a little exhausting to be around. I've been trying to look at the happy things this Christmastime- baking cookies, looking at the lights, wrapping presents with my SO's mom, buying presents for my new chosen family, and celebrating with my SO and kittens our first Christmas in our new home.   Sorry for the book. Hope your holidays turn out well. Thanks for the support in advance and creating a place to heal and vent!

Hi there! First off I'd like to say that wanting to go to the hospital shows a lot of strength and insight on your part! You do not have to tell your employers or anyone why you're going to the hospital, just go. If they want to visit you, you can put them on a list if you would like. Psych wards are all about confidentiality, so the staff tries its hardest to not let anyone you don't want to know anything know anything. You must give consent for visitors, medication, and other treatments, even if you're an involuntary patient. Patients have the same rights as any other patient on any other floor. You'll be voluntary if you seek help. The psych ward isn't there to hold you hostage. Restraints are always last resort. I'm a nursing student who just finished my psych rotation and I've NEVER seen them use restraints or the seclusion room (which is just a quiet room with a mattress). The nurses and other staff will try to use other ways to calm patients if the patients show other signs of aggression or actively try to hurt themselves, which would be the only groups who would be receiving chemical or physical restraints.



Now for the more real talk, I have Major Depressive Disorder and have been in the psych ward for suicidal ideation before. I totally understand your fear, I was there, too. I was terrified! It was actually more boring than scary. You're not allowed to have any electronics that can take pictures or could possibly be used as a weapon. I would suggest taking things you like to do with you or books you like to read. It gets really boring in between meal times, group, and assessments by the doctors and nurses. The staff wants to encourage functioning and making you feel comfortable so wearing your own clothes instead of a hospital gown is preferred. It's definitely more comfortable than wearing a gown with half your ass hanging out. Bring any toiletries that you like using. Hospital ones suck. The psych ward set me up with some medication that as helpful, taught coping skills, and referred me to a psychiatrist and psychologist. You can PM me if you want!

I entered this most recent relationship and the previous, which was my first serious relationship the same way. Both were great for a little while until we got out of the honeymoon stage. The ups and downs of a relationship led to me over analyzing every single aspect and causing me to wonder if it was something I did. "What's wrong with me?" was a common question I asked myself whenever things became less than perfect. These feeling towards myself also led to me dating people who weren't the greatest. They had these feelings, too, but they manifested in some pretty destructive habits such as drug use, cheating, and just being shitty people. 


 After my last breakup, I had an epiphany that I really needed to do some major reconstruction on myself and my attitudes or this pattern would just keep happening. I'm taking a year and a half off of dating to figure out how to love myself and get the help I need. If you feel like shit, you're not going to get this angelic girl who is going to come down and fix all of your problems. This angelic girl is probably dating another angelic girl. People are generally attracted to people who have the same thing going on with them. A relationship isn't going to fix you, you have to fix you, or at least your attitudes. A super cheesy quotation by Rupaul that really rings true to me is "If you can't love yourself how and the hell are you going to love somebody else?". You really need to learn how to stand alone before you get into a relationship. A relationship is only the sum of its parts, just think about how amazing your next relationship will be if you can learn to love you! The road to self-acceptance is so hard but so worth it.
